geometry.quote: The initial four H.E.S.S. telescopes (Phase I) are arranged in form of a square with 120 m side length. The diagonal of the square is oriented north-south.

method: Square of side 120 m, diagonal oriented north-south (both facts from the H.E.S.S. Telescopes page), computed by placing one vertex at each of bearings 0/90/180/270 degrees and distance 120*sqrt(2)/2 = 84.8528 m (spherical destination-point formula, R = 6371008.8 m) from the array's own official published coordinate (site:khomas-highland-hess, precision_m 200). accuracy_m is set equal to that anchor's own precision_m (200 m), satisfying the coarse-anchor rule exactly rather than claiming a false sub-200 m accuracy for where the square sits; the square's own shape (120 m side) is exact by construction from the sourced figure. No OpenStreetMap trace of the individual CT1-CT4 telescope pads could be attempted this session (Overpass refused every connection attempt, see worklog), which would otherwise have anchored the square far more tightly.
name: H.E.S.S. CT1-CT4 telescope square (120 m side, diagonal north-south)
notes: Positioned at the array's own official coordinate, not at an independently surveyed square centre; the square's internal geometry (120 m side, N-S diagonal) is exact, its placement on the ground carries the site point's own 200 m uncertainty. Individual CT1-CT4 identities/positions within the square are not distinguished (no source this session assigns a specific corner to a specific telescope number).

summary.plain: The square formed by H.E.S.S.'s original four 12 m telescopes, 120 metres to a side.
